title: Before the line stopped: Past Perfect
grammar: Past Perfect (had + particípio) — sequência de eventos
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Past Perfect (had + particípio) para mostrar que uma ação aconteceu antes de outra no passado. Vai conseguir explicar a ordem dos fatos numa parada de máquina ou numa investigação de falha — 'the fan had already stopped when we arrived' — algo essencial em relatórios de manutenção e passagens de turno na Delta Ducon.
intro: When you investigate a failure, order matters. What had happened before the line stopped? Had someone changed the pressure? Had the team cleaned the bags?
The Past Perfect (had + past participle) shows the earlier action of two past events. Today we use it to put a shift, a repair or a breakdown in the right order.
introAudio: Hi, I am Marcos. When I reached the shop floor last night, the fan had already stopped and the operators had left. Today we learn how to show which action happened first with the Past Perfect: had plus the past participle.
vocab: The breakdown happened after the belt had worn out.
The team had already fixed the fan when I arrived.
The ducts were clogged because dust had built up.
The bearing had worn out before the failure.
By the time we reached the site, the line had stopped.
practice: The ______ started after the belt had snapped.
When I arrived, the team had ______ left.
The duct was ______ because dust had built up.
The bearing had ______ before it seized.
By the time we ______ the plant, the fan had stopped.
The night shift had cleaned the bags before the ______.
The filter was ______ when the operator opened it.

audio.title: What had happened before we arrived
audio.text: By the time we reached the client site, the line had already stopped. The operator told us that the fan had made a strange noise for an hour. Before it failed, a bearing had worn out and the belt had snapped. The night shift had cleaned the filter bags, but nobody had checked the motor. We found that dust had built up inside the duct. Once we understood what had happened, we replaced the bearing and restarted the line.

readAloud: The fan had already stopped when we arrived.
The team had cleaned the bags before the shift ended.
The bearing had worn out before the failure.
Dust had built up inside the clogged duct.
Nobody had checked the motor before the breakdown.
fill: The fan had ___ when we arrived. (stop)
The team had ___ the bags before lunch. (clean)
The bearing had ___ out under load. (wear)
The belt had ___ before the failure. (break)
Dust had ___ up inside the duct. (build)
The operator had ___ the pressure earlier. (check)
We had ___ the report before the meeting. (write)
The client had ___ the drawings by Friday. (approve)
qa: What had happened before the line stopped?
A bearing had worn out and the belt had snapped.
Had the team cleaned the bags?
Yes, they had cleaned them before the shift ended.
Why was the duct clogged?
Because dust had built up over the week.
Had anyone checked the motor?
No, nobody had checked it before the breakdown.
What had you done before you restarted the line?
We had replaced the bearing and tested the fan.

b.label: Frase começando com By the time
b.placeholder: By the time we arrived, the line had stopped.

sentences: The fan had already stopped when we arrived.
The team had cleaned the bags before the shift ended.
A bearing had worn out before the belt snapped.
Dust had built up inside the clogged duct.
Nobody had checked the motor before the breakdown.
By the time we reached the site, the line had stopped.
We had written the report before the meeting started.
The client had approved the drawings before assembly began.
grammarPoint: O Past Perfect mostra que uma ação aconteceu antes de outra no passado. Forma: had + particípio (para todas as pessoas). The fan had stopped when we arrived. — O ventilador já tinha parado quando chegamos. Usamos o Past Simple para a ação mais recente e o Past Perfect para a mais antiga.
deepDive: Palavras como before, after, by the time, already e when ajudam a marcar a ordem. Atenção ao particípio: verbos regulares levam -ed (cleaned), mas os irregulares mudam (break -> broken, wear -> worn, build -> built). A forma curta é 'd: They'd left = They had left. Na negativa, use had not (hadn't): We hadn't checked the motor.
examples: The fan had stopped before we arrived.
O ventilador tinha parado antes de chegarmos.
They had already left when I called.
Eles já tinham saído quando liguei.
The bearing had worn out under load.
O rolamento tinha se desgastado sob carga.
Dust had built up inside the duct.
Poeira tinha se acumulado dentro do duto.
We had tested the line before startup.
Tínhamos testado a linha antes da partida.
The client had approved the drawings.
O cliente tinha aprovado os desenhos.
Nobody had checked the motor.
Ninguém tinha verificado o motor.
By the time we finished, the shift had ended.
Quando terminamos, o turno já tinha acabado.
mistakes: When we arrived, the fan has stopped.
When we arrived, the fan had stopped.
Para uma ação anterior no passado, use had + particípio, não has.
The team had clean the bags.
The team had cleaned the bags.
Depois de had vem o particípio, não a forma base.
The belt had broke before the failure.
The belt had broken before the failure.
O particípio de break é broken, não broke.
We had went to the site.
We had gone to the site.
O particípio de go é gone, não went.
By the time we arrived, dust builds up.
By the time we arrived, dust had built up.
A ação anterior pede Past Perfect: had built up.
quick: The fan had ___ when we arrived. (stop)
Dust had ___ up in the duct. (build)
We had ___ the report before the meeting. (write)

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now explain the exact order of events in a breakdown — the backbone of a clear failure report.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você consegue explicar a ordem exata dos eventos numa pane — a espinha dorsal de um bom relatório de falha.

title: How long it had been running: Past Perfect Continuous
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender o Past Perfect Continuous (had been + -ing) para falar de uma ação que vinha acontecendo por um tempo antes de outro momento no passado. Vai conseguir descrever por quanto tempo uma máquina vinha operando ou vibrando antes de falhar — 'the fan had been running for six hours before it overheated' — muito útil em análises de causa e relatórios de manutenção na Delta Ducon.
intro: Some failures build up slowly. The fan had been vibrating for days. The bearing had been overheating for hours before it seized.

The Past Perfect Continuous (had been + -ing) shows an action that had been in progress for a period before another past moment. Today we use it to describe how long something had been happening before it stopped or broke.
introAudio: Hi, I am Paula. The motor had been running for twelve hours before it overheated, and the fan had been vibrating all morning. Today we learn to say how long something had been happening in the past, with had been plus the -ing form.
vocab: The fan had been vibrating for hours before it failed.
The motor had been overheating since noon.
The scrubber had been leaking for two days.
The line had been running continuously all week.
The pump had been working for six hours.
The bearing had been overheating since morning.
practice: The fan had been starting to ______ before it failed.
The motor had begun to ______ under the heavy load.
The scrubber had a ______ near the bottom valve.
The line had been able to ______ all week.
The pump had been working ______ six hours.
The bearing had been getting hot ______ morning.
The duct had begun to ______ at the seams.
The team had been on site ______ two days.

audio.title: The fan that had been vibrating
audio.text: When the technicians opened the fan, they understood the problem. It had been vibrating for three days, but nobody had reported it. The bearing had been overheating since Monday, and the belt had been slipping for hours. The line had been running continuously all week without a proper inspection. The operators had been hearing a strange noise, yet they had kept the machine going. Because it had been working under stress for so long, the bearing finally seized.

readAloud: The fan had been vibrating for three days.
The motor had been overheating since Monday.
The scrubber had been leaking for two days.
The line had been running continuously all week.
The operators had been hearing a strange noise.
fill: The fan had been ___ for hours. (vibrate)
The motor had been ___ since noon. (overheat)
The scrubber had been ___ for two days. (leak)
The line had been ___ all week. (run)
The team had been ___ the machine. (test)
The operators had been ___ a strange noise. (hear)
The belt had been ___ for hours. (slip)
We had been ___ on the report all morning. (work)
qa: How long had the fan been vibrating?
It had been vibrating for three days.
Had the motor been overheating?
Yes, it had been overheating since Monday.
Why did the bearing seize?
Because it had been working under stress for too long.
What had the operators been hearing?
They had been hearing a strange noise.
How long had the line been running?
It had been running continuously all week.

b.label: Frase com 'for' ou 'since' (período)
b.placeholder: The motor had been running for six hours.

sentences: The fan had been vibrating for three days.
The motor had been overheating since Monday.
The scrubber had been leaking for two days.
The line had been running continuously all week.
The operators had been hearing a strange noise.
The belt had been slipping for hours before it broke.
We had been working on the report all morning.
The bearing had been getting hot since the early shift.
grammarPoint: O Past Perfect Continuous mostra uma ação que vinha acontecendo por um tempo antes de outro momento no passado. Forma: had been + verbo com -ing. The fan had been vibrating for hours before it failed. — O ventilador vinha vibrando havia horas antes de falhar. Enfatiza a duração da ação anterior.
deepDive: Use for para períodos (for two hours) e since para o ponto de início (since Monday). Diferença com o Past Perfect simples: 'had been running' foca na duração; 'had run' foca no resultado. Verbos de estado (know, be, have) normalmente não usam a forma contínua. Forma negativa: had not been working (hadn't been working).
examples: The fan had been vibrating for days.
O ventilador vinha vibrando havia dias.
The motor had been overheating since noon.
O motor vinha superaquecendo desde o meio-dia.
The scrubber had been leaking for two days.
O lavador vinha vazando havia dois dias.
The line had been running all week.
A linha vinha operando a semana toda.
We had been testing the fans since morning.
Vínhamos testando os ventiladores desde a manhã.
The belt had been slipping for hours.
A correia vinha patinando havia horas.
They had been working under stress for months.
Elas vinham trabalhando sob estresse havia meses.
The operators had been hearing that noise for days.
Os operadores vinham ouvindo aquele ruído havia dias.
mistakes: The fan had been vibrate for hours.
The fan had been vibrating for hours.
Depois de had been vem o verbo com -ing.
The motor has been overheating since Monday.
The motor had been overheating since Monday.
Para o passado, use had been, não has been.
The line had been running since three hours.
The line had been running for three hours.
Com um período usamos for, não since.
The team had been work all week.
The team had been working all week.
Falta o -ing: had been working.
It had been leak for two days.
It had been leaking for two days.
A forma correta é had been leaking.
quick: The fan had been ___ for hours. (vibrate)
The motor had been ___ since noon. (overheat)
The scrubber had been ___ for days. (leak)
The line had been ___ all week. (run)

celebrate.en: Excellent. You can now describe how long a machine had been struggling before it failed — a key detail in any root-cause analysis.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue descrever por quanto tempo uma máquina vinha sofrendo antes de falhar — um detalhe-chave em qualquer análise de causa raiz.

title: What must be done: passive with modals
grammar: Passiva com modais (must be / can be / should be + particípio)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a voz passiva com modais (must be / can be / should be + particípio) para dizer o que deve, pode ou deveria ser feito, sem focar em quem faz. Vai conseguir escrever instruções e procedimentos claros — 'the filter bags must be replaced', 'the panel should be locked out' — muito usado em manuais, checklists de segurança e a ISO 9001 na Delta Ducon.
intro: Procedures rarely say who does the work — they say what has to be done. The bags must be replaced. The pressure can be adjusted. The guard should be refitted.
That is the passive with modals: modal + be + past participle. Today we use it to write clear rules and steps for the shop floor and the job site.
introAudio: Hi, I am Rafael, site manager. In a procedure, the panel must be locked out before any repair, and the filter bags should be checked every shift. Today we learn the passive with modals: must be, can be and should be, plus the past participle.
vocab: The filter bags must be replaced every year.
The panel must be locked out before a repair.
The flow rate can be adjusted at the damper.
The ducts should be inspected every shift.
The bolts must be tightened to the correct torque.
The guard should be refitted after the repair.
practice: The worn bags must be ______ every year.
The panel must be ______ before any repair.
The flow rate can be ______ at the damper.
The ducts should be ______ every shift.
The bolts must be ______ to the correct torque.
The guard should be ______ after the job.
The gaskets must be ______ if they leak.
The pressure can be ______ from the control room.

audio.title: How the baghouse must be maintained
audio.text: A baghouse must be maintained on a strict schedule. The filter bags should be inspected every shift, and worn bags must be replaced at once. Before any internal work, the panel must be locked out and the fan must be stopped. The differential pressure can be adjusted at the control room, but it should be recorded in the log. All bolts must be tightened to the correct torque, and every guard should be refitted before startup. If these steps are followed, the emission limits can be met safely.

readAloud: The filter bags must be replaced every year.
The panel must be locked out before a repair.
The flow rate can be adjusted at the damper.
The ducts should be inspected every shift.
The guard should be refitted before startup.
fill: The bags must be ___ every year. (replace)
The panel must be ___ out first. (lock)
The flow rate can be ___ at the damper. (adjust)
The ducts should be ___ every shift. (inspect)
The bolts must be ___ to torque. (tighten)
The guard should be ___ after the job. (refit)
The pressure should be ___ in the log. (record)
The emission limit can be ___ safely. (meet)
qa: What must be done before a repair?
The panel must be locked out and the fan must be stopped.
How often should the bags be inspected?
They should be inspected every shift.
Can the flow rate be adjusted?
Yes, it can be adjusted at the damper.
What must be replaced when the bags are worn?
The worn bags must be replaced at once.
Where should the pressure be recorded?
It should be recorded in the log.
sentences: The filter bags must be replaced every year.
The panel must be locked out before a repair.
The flow rate can be adjusted at the damper.
The ducts should be inspected every shift.
The bolts must be tightened to the correct torque.
The guard should be refitted before startup.
The pressure can be adjusted from the control room.
The emission limits must be met at all times.
grammarPoint: A passiva com modais foca no que é feito, não em quem faz. Forma: modal (must / can / should) + be + particípio. The bags must be replaced. — As mangas devem ser substituídas. The flow can be adjusted. — O fluxo pode ser ajustado. É a forma padrão de manuais e procedimentos.
deepDive: O verbo be nunca muda depois do modal: sempre 'be' (não 'is' nem 'are'). Só o particípio carrega o sentido: locked, replaced, inspected, tightened. Na negativa: The panel must not be opened. Cuidado com particípios irregulares: meet -> met, do -> done, take -> taken. Compare ativa e passiva: 'You must replace the bags' = 'The bags must be replaced'.
examples: The bags must be replaced.
As mangas devem ser substituídas.
The panel must be locked out.
O painel deve ser bloqueado.
The flow can be adjusted.
O fluxo pode ser ajustado.
The ducts should be inspected.
Os dutos deveriam ser inspecionados.
The bolts must be tightened.
Os parafusos devem ser apertados.
The guard should be refitted.
A proteção deveria ser recolocada.
The panel must not be opened.
O painel não deve ser aberto.
The report should be signed by the supervisor.
O relatório deveria ser assinado pelo supervisor.
mistakes: The bags must replaced every year.
The bags must be replaced every year.
Falta o 'be': modal + be + particípio.
The panel must be lock out.
The panel must be locked out.
Depois de be usamos o particípio: locked.
The flow can be adjust at the damper.
The flow can be adjusted at the damper.
O particípio é adjusted, não a forma base.
The ducts should are inspected.
The ducts should be inspected.
Depois do modal usamos be, nunca are.
The limit must be meeted.
The limit must be met.
O particípio de meet é met, é irregular.

celebrate.en: Great job. You can now write clear procedures and rules in the passive — exactly how professional manuals and ISO documents read.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você consegue escrever procedimentos e regras na voz passiva — exatamente como leem os manuais profissionais e os documentos ISO.

title: Passing on orders: told, asked and warned
grammar: Ordens reportadas (told / asked / warned + to + infinitivo)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a reportar ordens e pedidos com told, asked e warned + to + infinitivo. Vai conseguir repassar instruções que você recebeu ou deu — 'the supervisor told us to stop the fan', 'they warned us not to enter' — habilidade central em passagens de turno, coordenação de equipe e registros de segurança na Delta Ducon.
intro: On site, instructions travel from person to person. The supervisor told us to stop the line. The client asked us to send the report. The safety officer warned everyone not to enter.
To pass on an order, we use told, asked or warned + someone + to + verb. Today we practise reporting instructions clearly and safely on the shop floor.
introAudio: Hi, I am Sofia, safety coordinator. This morning the supervisor told the team to lock out the panel, and I asked the operators to check their PPE. I also warned them not to enter the confined space alone. Today we learn to report orders with told, asked and warned plus to and the verb.
vocab: The supervisor told us to stop the fan.
The client asked us to send the report.
They warned us not to enter the area.
The manager reminded the team to sign the permit.
The order was to shut down the line.
The instruction was clear and easy to follow.
practice: The supervisor will ______ the team to stop the fan.
The client may ______ us to send the report today.
The officer had to ______ them not to enter.
Please ______ the crew to sign the permit.
The ______ was to shut down the whole line.
The ______ on the sign was easy to follow.
Did anyone ______ the operator to lock it out?
We had to ______ the visitors to wear helmets.

audio.title: The orders during the shutdown
audio.text: During the shutdown, everyone had a job. The supervisor told the operators to stop the fan and lock out the panel. He asked the maintenance team to replace the worn bearing. The safety officer warned the visitors not to enter the marked area. The client asked us to send a report before the end of the day. I reminded the crew to sign the work permit first. Because everyone followed the instructions, the shutdown finished safely and on time.

readAloud: The supervisor told us to stop the fan.
The client asked us to send the report.
The officer warned them not to enter the area.
The manager reminded the team to sign the permit.
He told the operators to lock out the panel.
fill: The supervisor told us ___ stop the fan. (to)
The client asked us to ___ the report. (send)
The officer warned them not to ___. (enter)
He told the operator to ___ out the panel. (lock)
I reminded the crew to ___ the permit. (sign)
They asked the team to ___ the bearing. (replace)
She warned us not to ___ the guard. (remove)
The manager told everyone to ___ their PPE. (wear)
qa: What did the supervisor tell the team to do?
He told them to stop the fan and lock out the panel.
What did the client ask you to do?
The client asked us to send the report by the end of the day.
What did the safety officer warn them about?
He warned them not to enter the marked area.
Did you remind the crew about the permit?
Yes, I reminded them to sign the work permit first.
What did the manager tell everyone to wear?
He told everyone to wear their PPE.

a.label: told / asked + someone + to + verbo
a.placeholder: The supervisor told us to stop the fan.

b.label: warned + someone + not to + verbo
b.placeholder: They warned us not to enter.

sentences: The supervisor told us to stop the fan.
The client asked us to send the report today.
The officer warned them not to enter the area.
The manager reminded the team to sign the permit.
He told the operators to lock out the panel.
They asked the crew to replace the worn bearing.
She warned us not to remove the guard.
The engineer told everyone to wear their PPE.
grammarPoint: Para reportar uma ordem ou pedido, use tell / ask / warn + alguém + to + verbo. The supervisor told us to stop the fan. — O supervisor mandou a gente parar o ventilador. Para o negativo, use not to: They warned us not to enter. — Eles nos avisaram para não entrar.
deepDive: Told e asked sempre pedem um objeto: told US to stop, asked THEM to wait (não 'told to stop'). Warn combina bem com not to para perigo: warned us not to touch. No passado: tell -> told, o pedido em si fica sempre em to + verbo base. Diferença: say não leva objeto assim (não 'said us to'); prefira told nesses casos.
examples: The supervisor told us to stop the fan.
O supervisor mandou a gente parar o ventilador.
The client asked us to send the report.
O cliente pediu que enviássemos o relatório.
The officer warned them not to enter.
O responsável avisou para eles não entrarem.
He told the operators to lock out the panel.
Ele mandou os operadores bloquear o painel.
I reminded the crew to sign the permit.
Lembrei a equipe de assinar a permissão.
They asked us to wait for the crane.
Eles pediram que esperássemos o guindaste.
She warned us not to remove the guard.
Ela nos avisou para não retirar a proteção.
The engineer told everyone to wear PPE.
O engenheiro mandou todos usarem EPI.
mistakes: The supervisor told to stop the fan.
The supervisor told us to stop the fan.
Told precisa de um objeto: told us, told them.
He asked us stop the line.
He asked us to stop the line.
Falta o 'to' antes do verbo.
They warned us to not enter.
They warned us not to enter.
A ordem certa é 'not to', não 'to not'.
The client said us to send the report.
The client asked us to send the report.
Com objeto e 'to', use asked ou told, não said.
He told us to stopped the fan.
He told us to stop the fan.
Depois de 'to' vem a forma base: stop.
quick: The supervisor told us ___ stop the fan. (to)
The client asked us to ___ the report. (send)
He told the crew to ___ the panel. (lock)
I reminded them to ___ the permit. (sign)

celebrate.en: Strong work. You can now pass on orders and warnings accurately in English — the glue that keeps a shift and a site safe.
celebrate.pt: Belo trabalho. Agora você consegue repassar ordens e avisos com precisão em inglês — a cola que mantém um turno e uma obra em segurança.

title: It must have failed: deducing the past
grammar: Dedução sobre o passado — must have / can't have / might have
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a deduzir sobre o passado com must have, can't have e might have + particípio. Vai conseguir levantar hipóteses numa investigação de falha — 'the bearing must have overheated', 'it can't have been the belt', 'someone might have skipped the check' — habilidade central em análise de causa raiz e reuniões técnicas na Delta Ducon.
intro: When a machine fails, you weigh the evidence. The bearing must have overheated. It can't have been the power supply. Someone might have skipped the inspection.
To deduce about the past we use must have, can't have and might have + past participle. Today we turn clues on the shop floor into confident and careful conclusions.
introAudio: Hi, I am Diego. Looking at the burnt bearing, I think the fan must have overheated during the night. It can't have been a power failure, because the log is clean. Someone might have missed the greasing. Today we learn to deduce about the past with must have, can't have and might have.
vocab: The main cause must have been a lack of lubrication.
The evidence shows the belt can't have failed first.
The failure might have started at the bearing.
Someone might have skipped the daily check.
The bearing must have run without lubrication.
The log shows it can't have been a power cut.
practice: The main ______ must have been a lack of grease.
The ______ shows it can't have been the belt.
The ______ might have started at the bearing.
Someone might have decided to ______ the daily check.
The bearing must have run without ______.
The ______ shows the fan ran all night.
We still don't know the exact ______ of the failure.
There is no ______ of a power cut.

audio.title: What must have caused the failure
audio.text: Looking at the damage, we tried to work out what had gone wrong. The bearing was blue with heat, so it must have overheated for hours. It can't have been a power cut, because the log shows the fan ran all night. Someone might have skipped the greasing on the last shift, or the grease line might have been blocked. The belt looked fine, so the belt can't have failed first. Our best guess is that the bearing must have run without enough lubrication until it seized.

readAloud: The bearing must have overheated during the night.
It can't have been a power cut.
Someone might have skipped the greasing.
The belt can't have failed first.
The grease line might have been blocked.
fill: The bearing must have ___ for hours. (overheat)
It can't have ___ a power cut. (be)
Someone might have ___ the daily check. (skip)
The grease line might have been ___. (block)
The operator must have ___ the noise. (hear)
They might have ___ the wrong part. (fit)
The fan must have ___ all night. (run)
qa: What must have caused the failure?
The bearing must have overheated from a lack of lubrication.
Can it have been a power cut?
No, it can't have been a power cut; the log is clean.
What might someone have skipped?
Someone might have skipped the greasing on the last shift.
Can the belt have failed first?
No, the belt looked fine, so it can't have failed first.
What might have blocked the grease?
The grease line might have been blocked.

b.label: Hipótese possível (might have + particípio)
b.placeholder: Someone might have skipped the check.

sentences: The bearing must have overheated during the night.
It can't have been a power cut.
Someone might have skipped the greasing.
The belt can't have failed first.
The grease line might have been blocked.
The operator must have heard the noise.
They might have fitted the wrong part.
The fan must have run all night without stopping.
grammarPoint: Para deduzir sobre o passado usamos modal + have + particípio. Must have = certeza (deve ter): The bearing must have overheated. — O rolamento deve ter superaquecido. Can't have = impossível (não pode ter): It can't have been the belt. — Não pode ter sido a correia. Might have = possibilidade (pode ter): Someone might have skipped the check. — Alguém pode ter pulado a verificação.
deepDive: A estrutura é sempre have + particípio, nunca 'had': must have been, não 'must had been'. Na fala vira 'must've', 'might've' — cuidado para não escrever 'must of'. Use must have para conclusão forte, might/could have para hipótese aberta, e can't have para descartar algo. O particípio de irregulares muda: be -> been, run -> run, hear -> heard.
examples: The bearing must have overheated.
O rolamento deve ter superaquecido.
It can't have been a power cut.
Não pode ter sido uma queda de energia.
Someone might have skipped the check.
Alguém pode ter pulado a verificação.
The belt can't have failed first.
A correia não pode ter falhado primeiro.
The grease line might have been blocked.
A linha de graxa pode ter ficado bloqueada.
They must have fitted the wrong seal.
Eles devem ter colocado a vedação errada.

mistakes: The bearing must overheated.

Falta o 'have': must have + particípio.

It can't have been a power cut.
Depois de have vem o particípio: been.

O particípio de skip é skipped.
The belt must had failed.
The belt must have failed.
É must have, nunca 'must had'.

Escreve-se 'must have', não 'must of'.
